## BundleArchive

```python
class BundleArchive
BundleArchive()
```

A deterministic gzipped tar of a directory, manifest at its root.

### BundleArchive.write()

```python
@staticmethod
def write(staging: Path, out: Path) -> bytes
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `staging` | `Path` | required | The directory whose files make the archive; each file lands in it at its own path under ``staging``. |
| `out` | `Path` | required | The path the archive is written to; its directory is made if it is not there. |

Write `staging`'s files to `out` as a gzipped tar and answer its bytes.

The same files make the same bytes every time: sorted, with no times,
owners or modes of their own.

### BundleArchive.read_manifest()

```python
@staticmethod
def read_manifest(archive: bytes) -> dict[str, object]
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `archive` | `bytes` | required | The bundle's bytes: the gzipped tar to read the manifest out of. |

The `manifest.json` at an archive's root, read without unpacking it.

Left as the JSON object it is: each reader validates it into its
own model. Raises `BundleError` when the archive is unreadable, has
no manifest at its root, or its manifest is not a JSON object.

igni's side of `host.agent(producer)`: the items, files and statuses a service sends.

`fake.agents.items` is every item stored, `uploads` every file, and
`settle(event_id, state)` plays the producer's igni taking one. Set
`grants` to play an extension that declares less.

Every igni endpoint a service calls, composed of one collaborator per part of igni.

### FakeIgni.router

```python
@property
router: FakeRouter
```

The pipeline every request the service sends goes through, as igni's router.

Made from the fake's collaborators as they are now, so a test that
replaces one (`fake.traffic = RecordedTraffic()`) is heard on the
wire, as it was when the pipeline was `FakeIgni`'s own.

### FakeIgni.reset()

```python
def reset() -> None
```

Forget what happened, keep who exists.

For a fake shared across a session: requests, failures, grants,
revoked tokens, sign-ins (codes and refresh tokens), notifications,
deliveries, the once-per-event memory, revocations, agent items and
held uploads go; organisations, members, registered clients, keys,
uploaded extensions and assets stay, so the next test starts from
the same world. Issued service and app tokens and used `jti`s stay
too: a service shared across the session may still hold a cached
token, and replay memory is never forgotten.

```python
    settings: IgniSettings | None = None,

    key_store: KeyStore | None = None,

) -> IgniService
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `settings` | `IgniSettings \| None` | `None` | The settings the service is made with; the fake's own, pointing at it, by default. |

| `clock` | `Clock \| None` | `None` | The clock the service reads the time from for its tokens' age and expiry. |
| `accepted_callers` | `Collection[CallerKind]` | `frozenset({CallerKind.PERSON})` | Whose tokens the service's ``caller`` accepts: people only, unless the service is told more. |

An `IgniService` wired to this fake: key in memory, retries without waiting.

### FakeIgni.upload()

```python
async def upload(
    bundle: str | Path | ExtensionBundle,
    service: IgniService,
) -> HeldExtension
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `bundle` | `str \| Path \| ExtensionBundle` | required | The extension's bundle: a built archive, the extension's directory, or the ``ExtensionBundle`` already built. |
| `service` | `IgniService` | required | The service that ships the bundle, and whose registration the upload is made under. |

Upload an extension as `service` does at start-up: registered, signed, over the wire.

`bundle` is a built `extension-bundle.tar.gz`, or an extension's
directory — its `manifest.json`, `README.md`, `plugin/` and `ui/` are
archived as they are, with no wheelhouse, which is all this fake
reads. Answers what the fake now holds (or holds back, with
`extensions.hold`). For a test that needs the extension on igni —
its VM profile request, its pages — without a lifespan or a build.

### FakeVmProfiles.approve()

## SettingsOverrides

```python
class SettingsOverrides(BaseModel)
SettingsOverrides(
    *,
    igni_server_url: str = '',
    public_base_url: str = '',
    service_name: str = '',
    client_kind: str = 'service',
    redirect_uris: list[str] = <factory>,
    key_encryption_key: str = '',
    key_database_url: str = '',
    extension_bundle_path: str = '',
    revocations_max_staleness: float = 30.0,
    timeout: float = 10.0,
)
```

What a test changes about the settings a service is wired to the fake with.

Only the fields a test sets are applied (`exclude_unset`): every other
one is the fake's address, its URL for the service, or `IgniSettings`'
own default. A field `IgniSettings` lacks is refused, not ignored.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `igni_server_url` | `str` | `''` | `IGNI_SERVER_URL`; the fake's address unless set. |
| `public_base_url` | `str` | `''` | `PUBLIC_BASE_URL`; `http://service.test` unless set. |
| `service_name` | `str` | `''` | `SERVICE_NAME`. |
| `client_kind` | `str` | `'service'` | `IGNI_CLIENT_KIND`: `service`. |
| `redirect_uris` | `list[str]` | factory | `IGNI_REDIRECT_URIS`: more addresses igni may send a signed-in person back to. |
| `key_encryption_key` | `str` | `''` | `IGNI_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. |
| `key_database_url` | `str` | `''` | `IGNI_KEY_DATABASE_URL`. |
| `extension_bundle_path` | `str` | `''` | `IGNI_EXTENSION_BUNDLE_PATH`: the bundle the service uploads at start-up. |
| `revocations_max_staleness` | `float` | `30.0` | `IGNI_REVOCATIONS_MAX_STALENESS`, in seconds. |
| `timeout` | `float` | `10.0` | `IGNI_SERVER_TIMEOUT`: each call to igni, in seconds. |

### SettingsOverrides.settings_for()

```python
def settings_for(addresses: IgniAddresses) -> IgniSettings
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `addresses` | `IgniAddresses` | required | The fake's addresses: where the service reaches the fake, and the URL the service's own tokens are for. |

Settings that reach the fake at `addresses`, with what this sets.

## TokenOverrides

```python
class TokenOverrides(BaseModel)
TokenOverrides(
    *,
    aud: str | None = None,
    iss: str | None = None,
    use: str | None = None,
    sub: str | None = None,
    org: str | None = None,
    kid: str | None = None,
    key: igni_service.crypto.RsaKeyPair | None = None,
    lifetime: float | datetime.timedelta | None = None,
)
```

What a test changes about a token; `None` is "as igni would sign it".

`org=""` is a change (a token for no organisation), which is why every
field is optional rather than defaulted.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `aud` | `str \| None` | `None` | Another audience: a token for another service. |
| `iss` | `str \| None` | `None` | Another issuer: a token somebody other than igni signed. |
| `use` | `str \| None` | `None` | Another `token_use`: the wrong kind of token. |
| `sub` | `str \| None` | `None` | Another subject. |
| `org` | `str \| None` | `None` | Another organisation; an empty string is a token for none. |
| `kid` | `str \| None` | `None` | Another key id in the header: a key igni does not publish. |
| `key` | `RsaKeyPair \| None` | `None` | Another key to sign with: a signature igni's keys do not verify. |
| `lifetime` | `float \| timedelta \| None` | `None` | How long it lives, in seconds or as a `timedelta`; negative is already expired. |

### TokenOverrides.seconds()

```python
def seconds(default: float) -> float
```

| Parameter | Type | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `default` | `float` | required | The lifetime to answer with when the test changed none: how long the token lives otherwise. |

The lifetime in seconds, or `default` when not changed.
